db.js:9-10,61-62; solve.sh:35). DEFECT: hireops_rules.md section 1 states 'A candidate who asks about an application that is not theirs is told it does not exist (404), so they cannot learn that it does.' The reference only honours this on the conversation routes (index.js:121-131). POST /api/applications/:id/move (index.js:324-327) and POST /api/moves/bulk (index.js:328-332) use auth() with no role restriction; moveCards looks the application up first and returns 404 'No such application.' when absent (index.js:277-278) and only then reaches checkMove's role check, returning 403 'Your role cannot move candidates.' (index.js:239). So a signed-in candidate can distinguish an existing other-person application (403) from a nonexistent id (404); seed ids are sequential (APP-101, APP-102, ...), so enumeration is trivial. The scripted golden only asserts the 404 on GET /api/applications/APP-201/messages (qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/workspace.cjs:188), not on move/bulk. Every screen and flow otherwise exists; this is a partial implementation of a stated privacy rule, found by code trace, not by a run.
counterexample: Sign in as noor.haddad@candidates.example, then POST /api/applications/APP-201/move with {"version":1,"to_stage":"SCREEN"}: the reference answers 403 'Your role cannot move candidates.' (application exists, belongs to someone else). POST /api/applications/APP-999/move with the same body answers 404 'No such application.' The difference reveals that APP-201 exists, contrary to hireops_rules.md section 1. Same via POST /api/moves/bulk with items naming two ids. (Code-traced from index.js:239,277-278,324-332; not executed in this review: no Docker run was started and no local express/better-sqlite3 install was used.)
suggested_fix: In the move and bulk-move routes, refuse candidates (and other non-movers) before looking up the application, or answer 404 for a candidate whenever the application is not theirs, and add that case to the scripted golden check.
